 Jeep China Recalls Wrangler and Gladiator for Power Steering Failure and Fire Risk
 A connector defect could leave Chinese drivers without power steering assistance. An overheating condition near the power steering pump is also possible 
 Published: 8 Nov 2026, 15:55 UTC 
 By: 
 Mircea Panait 
   86 photos Photo: Jeep / edited 
 The Jeep brand is recalling a bunch of imported Wrangler and Gladiator models in China. Two companies handle the Jeep recall, which totals 28,156 vehicles. These body-on-frame SUVs and pickups are fitted with an electrical connector that may not work as intended, potentially disabling power steering assistance. 
 If the defective connection overheats, you can easily guess what happens next. Split between Stellantis Automotive and Chrysler Automotive Sales, the campaign includes 24,492 examples of the Wrangler and 3,664 of the Gladiator, all imported from the Toledo complex in the United States of America.
 Filed with China's State Administration for Market Regulation, these recalls take effect immediately. The Auburn Hills-based automaker previously manufactured and distributed production models through GAC Fiat Chrysler Automobiles, but said arrangement eventually unraveled. Local production stopped in January 2022, leading to a bankruptcy filing in October 2022.
 The last models Jeep assembled in China prior to the dissolution of the local joint venture were the Grand Commander, Cherokee, Compass, and Renegade. Never sold in the US, the Grand Commander in question is a mid-size crossover with three-row seating. Unfortunately, it never sold well.
 Turning our attention back to the recall, the electrical connection issue concerns the electro-hydraulic power steering pump. Due to a manufacturing defect, the pins inside the electrical connector may not be arranged correctly, preventing the connector from establishing a reliable electrical connection.
 Photo: Jeep 
A power steering system that loses electrical communication with the pump obviously loses power assistance. That scenario is especially dangerous when driving at high speeds, more so when you remember that there is no warning to speak of. Defective connections also have the ability to generate excessive heat around the connector and nearby components, increasing the risk of a fire.
 S2026M0122V is the SAMR number for the Chrysler Automotive Sales campaign, which includes 18,544 units of the Wrangler and 1,853 of the Gladiator. These vehicles were produced from August 2020 through August 2024 and January 2022 through September 2022, respectively.
 Stellantis Automotive is the legal entity that handles campaign number S2026M0123V. Its population covers 5,948 examples of the Wrangler from June 2023 through October 2024 and 1,811 units of the Gladiator manufactured between April 2023 and December 2023. While the production windows may overlap, bear in mind that both distributors have separate populations.
 Dealers are to inspect the connection between the electro-hydraulic power steering pump and its wiring harness. Service techs must check if the connector and pump-end interface engage as intended. They also have to check that both retaining mechanisms, the secondary lock, and the connector latch do their jobs properly.
 If the connection fails these checks, both the wiring harness and the power steering pump will be replaced. In the near future, customers will be notified by Chrysler Automotive Sales and Stellantis Automotive by telephone and SMS.
